01 / BOUNDARY

Let agents work.Keep the keys.

Isolated tasks

Two layers of isolation: each task runs in its own cell inside a local VM.

Protected credentials

Trusted services use real credentials outside the sandbox.

Access and approvals

Set folder, connector and network access: GitHub, AWS, Linear, PostHog, Sentry, Firecrawl, Figma, Discord, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion and Slack. Listed high-risk writes wait by default; explicit exceptions can bypass that default.

[i]

Credential isolation is not data isolation. What an agent reads can still reach a cloud model. Security model ↗

05 / BEFORE YOU START

What to expect.

Do I need a Codex account?

Connect one runtime: Codex, Claude Code or Hermes. The builder uses whichever runtime is connected, and a starter agent can be created without any model call; a hand-written agent file works too. First-task guide ↗

How much setup and disk space does it need?

Install Lima and Python (plus QEMU/KVM on Linux). Setup creates a VM with half your host's CPUs and memory by default, and lets you change that. Keep at least 8 GB free for installation and more for images and projects. First setup and the first runtime build take several minutes.

Does all my data stay on my computer?

No. Managed credentials stay outside task cells, but content can reach the model and permitted destinations. Omitting egress allows public Internet access. An egress list always permits runtime and configured connector hosts; Firecrawl can fetch URLs outside it.

Is this ready for sensitive production accounts?

Release packages are not signed yet. If that matters to you, build and run Anchi from source, the desktop app included (scripts/anchi-desktop), so what runs is code you can review. Anchi has not completed a third-party security audit; before connecting sensitive production accounts, try the authorization and approval flow with test accounts. Model calls use your subscription quota or API credit.

Where do I find docs, upgrades or help?

Documentation · Release notes · Report a problem. Check release notes for required VM updates after updating the app. Report vulnerabilities privately.
